Consider the diagram shown above, where $\overset{\to }{DA}=a,$ $\overset{\to }{AB}=b,$ $\overset{\to }{BC}=c,$ and $\overset{\to }{DE}=d.$ Find $\overset{\to }{DC}$ in terms of vectors $a,b,c,$ and $d.$ To denote the corresponding vectors, use $a$, $b,$ $c,$ and $d.$

$\overset{\to }{DC}=$  
 {{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
We want to find a "path" from $D$ to $C$ consisting only of the vectors $a,b,c,$ and $d.$

According to the triangle law of addition,

$$
\overset{\to }{DC}=\overset{\to }{DA}+\overset{\to }{AB}+\overset{\to }{BC}
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14212914/assets/cd94c2f43b5da5252879f8acdcc14fc2f951f9a899903482bd3947ca8ec6921e.png)

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
\overset{\to }{DA}=a,\,\overset{\to }{AB}=b,\,\overset{\to }{BC}=c.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14212914/assets/e0f53eb04be491e8b84e2c7d5d252ab2c04bdfe372a93a503788a1ee94f63675.png)

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{DC} & =\overset{\to }{DA}+\overset{\to }{AB}+\overset{\to }{BC} \\  & =a+b+c.\end{aligned}
$$
